Outbound read_transfer_chunk marksCompleted as soon as requested index is final, before websocket send and without receiver acknowledgment. Send failure then disconnect cleanup only requeuesSending, leavingCompleted. UI completion is not proof remote file saved.

Outbound permits any in-range chunk index and computes progress from requested offset, not unique delivered chunks. Requesting final first can markCompleted and block earlier requests. No actual phone/protocol execution in this batch.

Inbound enforces in-order chunks, duplicate rejection, exact decoded size and correct done flag, and tracks received count beforeCompleted. This is stronger local byte coverage than outbound; no file checksum/fsync/atomic staging rename before completion.

Inbound writes directly to final visible destination, leaves partial file on failure/disconnect, and has no resume/requeue transition forReceiving. Duplicate transfer id remains in memory, hindering restart until state cleared. No user files created.

Outbound disconnect requeuesSending but preserves assigned_device_id, allowing same device selection after reconnect. Start resets all transfer state; no persistent queue. Completed/failed entries retained until outbound cap drain or restart.
Outbound queue cap20 drains oldest entries regardless status, potentially forgetting active inbound/outbound entries. Incoming manifest append has no corresponding cap; count limit not universal.
